growth_formula_finding: The PLANNED form is the primary prospective verdict; the lag form is a secondary additional prediction. Legacy pairs fit the lag form within 160MiB, while the planned form fails at multi-doubling sizes. A one-chunk realization lag is a hypothesis explaining this pattern, not a measured fact.

hypotheses.evidence: ES accepted records give matched observe-minus-eval-pool gaps for a single measured request (pre-existing SUPPORTED verdict, unchanged); chunk-resolved D_j pairing computed above is retrospective. The historical two-request (#406) growth lacks any between-request sample, so q2 carryover is not identifiable offline.
hypotheses.mechanism: lazy-scatter / version pinning (WP1 H4; diagnosis H1)
hypotheses.missing: per-request q2 pairing with matched eval-pool, planned live

hypotheses.evidence: mx.cache counters before/after per-chunk clear are reported per intervention; cache counters are not a unique resident-footprint partition.
hypotheses.missing: clear-cache vs observe pairs at matched chunks (live 16k stage)

hypotheses.evidence: req_caches_by_id/cache_pool_len traces are reported; metadata bytes alias active bytes and are never added; no-radix has no shared pool; whether the small 128MiB term is a retained small cache is tested only through the trace, not proven.
hypotheses.mechanism: parked / private KV cache (WP1 H3; diagnosis H6) and pool realization (diagnosis H3)

hypotheses.evidence: needs_logits=false is intent; _forward_lazy_token falls back to full forward when _trunk_forward returns None (see source line hits); peak-minus-active is not a logits allocation measurement.
hypotheses.mechanism: logits / final-chunk transients (WP1 H2; diagnosis H4)

hypotheses.evidence: interval maxima, post-finish decode steps and release windows bound a transient versus retention only.
role contributions from synchronized tree samples; footprint-active-cache is a diagnostic proxy across incompatible domains.

engine_log_corroboration.resolution: second-resolution; not a unique request join

operands.F0_definition: last server_rss sample before request1 start (after-load/after-warmup plateau); the engine log's own `Memory baseline taken` reads 0.00 GB and is a different domain
operands.max_peak_note: peak_bytes is the kernel lifetime maximum reported with each sample; it need not coincide with a sampled footprint; the issue's >=33.412GiB is this lifetime-maximum quantity

qualifications: request2 prompt count 32768 is the client's expected count, not confirmed server usage; its cached_tokens is null
prefix32 and an exact request2 new-token count are inference, not ground truth
the issue's '32960' wording is a different quantity from raw observed request1 input 32802
no footprint sample lies between request1 completion and request2 growth
QB footprint is a whole-engine sum in the QB probe's domain; ES scheduler-only and tree sums use different baselines
